findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued is frozen at import time
findings.body: AssignmentSource.queued is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class body is executed, not on each construction, and datetime is not a default_factory. Every AssignmentSource created via from_integration or from_dict without an explicit queued value therefore shares the single timestamp captured when the module was imported. The field is meant to record when that assignment change was queued and is copied into every outbound task payload via to_dict, but rapid successive assignee updates (the case this PR is fixing) are indistinguishable by time, and freeze_time in tests cannot affect it. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each source gets its own timestamp.

findings.title: AssignmentSource dict is not a safe Celery payload
findings.body: to_dict() is dataclasses.asdict, so the dict passed to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async in sync_group_assignee_outbound includes queued as a raw datetime. That task previously accepted only ints, a bool, and None. A datetime is not JSON-serializable: under a JSON task serializer, apply_async raises TypeError while handling the inbound webhook, after GroupAssignee.assign/deassign has already written the assignee. The webhook then errors, linked integrations other than the source never get the update, and retries repeat the failure. from_dict is also not an inverse of to_dict: it splats the dict into the constructor and only catches TypeError/ValueError, so an ISO-string queued value is accepted as a str rather than parsed, and any malformed payload returns None. The outbound task treats None as "no source" and calls should_sync without a source, which re-enables the echo and brings the sync loop back. Eager task tests never cross this serialization boundary, so they do not catch it.

findings.title: Cross-integration and deassign cycle behavior untested
findings.body: The new test only assigns with AssignmentSource.from_integration on the same integration that owns the single linked external issue and asserts sync_assignee_outbound is not called. Nothing covers a second linked integration with a different id, which is the case the change claims must still propagate, so a regression that skips every outbound sync whenever any AssignmentSource is present would still pass. Inbound deassign now also threads assignment_source through GroupAssignee.deassign, but the deassign test still only expects assignment_source=None and never asserts that a matching source suppresses the outbound unassign. Both paths are required to stop the Jira assignee loop.
